intent.goal: Close the sidecar-CREATION race left by #393: a pre-#388 writer that creates and locks <manifest>.lock after the new wrapper's absence check must not silently lose a record. The fix must not create the sidecar and must keep the one lock order.
intent.ruled_out: Creating the sidecar when absent (#388 litter and fingerprint drift; spec scope (a)). Waiting on the sidecar while holding the manifest lock: ABBA against a new writer that joined the sidecar and waits on the manifest (spec scope (b)). Re-checking only right after the manifest lock, the spec's suggested point: that leaves the read, parse and serialize inside the residual gap, and the pre-truncate look already covers every sidecar that appears earlier, since legacy writers never remove theirs. A post-write verify-and-reappend: it needs a record identity the ledger lacks (two same-second runs of one command write byte-identical records), adds a second retry loop, and only narrows a gap that is already a few syscalls wide. Accept-with-reason alone (coordinator-declined in the spec). Lock-free peers (impossible, spec scope note).
intent.why: Legacy writers go create -> lock -> read -> write, and never remove the sidecar (e04b0c2 opens it 'a' and leaves it). So if no sidecar exists at the moment just before this append truncates, no legacy writer has read the manifest yet, and if one exists, rejoining it waits out any legacy read-modify-write in flight. Looking as late as possible makes the unguarded span the smallest it can be without creating the file: seek, truncate, one write. The rejoin reuses sidecar_lock and the existing `with`, so the lock order holds by construction.

decisions: 2026-09-15: preconditions asserted before the first commit: branch ravidsrk/u393-race, HEAD 62da77c, `git status --porcelain` empty, spec sha256 7565569e... matches the contract digest.

Methodology: the `tdd` skill only (red-first, one slice). The seam is the one the frozen spec names for C-1, 'all locking/IO through the real module functions': the module-level append_record, loaded by path. The only reach inside is two delegating stand-ins (mock.patch.object on the module's `fcntl` and `json` names) that pause and never replace. Disclosed coupling: the pause points are fcntl.flock and json.loads. A future fix that stopped calling both would stall the schedule, and the test would FAIL on its liveness bound, not pass.

Threads, not processes, carry the two writers so the barriers can be threading.Events with no file polling. flock is per open file description: a probe showed a second open() in the same process BLOCKED on the first's LOCK_EX (macOS, Python 3.13.15).

The re-check point improves on the suggested shape: immediately before the truncate, not right after the manifest lock. Same rejoin mechanics and lock order, and a smaller residual (see intent.ruled_out and noticed_not_touched).

REJOIN_ATTEMPTS = 3: legacy writers never remove the sidecar, so the second attempt holds it. The bound only matters if a third party deletes and recreates the file, and the last attempt writes regardless, per the spec's 'bounded retries, then proceed'.

RESIDUAL window, stated for adjudication: see noticed_not_touched[0] and the append_record docstring. The builder judges it acceptable: it is syscall-width, it cannot be closed under #388, and C-1's forced schedule, the natural shape of the race, is closed.
